import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "crypto";

export interface VerifyOptions {
  toleranceSeconds?: number;
}

// Verifies "t=<unix>,v1=<hex>" signature header over `${t}.${rawBody}`
export function verifySignature(
  rawBody: string,
  header: string,
  secret: string,
  opts: VerifyOptions = {}
): boolean {
  const tolerance = opts.toleranceSeconds ?? 300;
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(
    header.split(",").map((p) => p.split("=") as [string, string])
  );
  const t = parseInt(parts["t"], 10);
  const sig = parts["v1"];
  if (!t || !sig) return false;

  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  if (Math.abs(now - t) > tolerance) return false;

  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(`${t}.${rawBody}`)
    .digest("hex");

  const a = Buffer.from(expected, "hex");
  const b = Buffer.from(sig, "hex");
  if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}

- `verify.ts` splits on `,` and `=` naively. HMAC is computed over `t.rawBody`, timing-safe comparison, tolerance check present. The `=` split truncates values containing `=`, but hex sigs don't contain `=`, so that's low impact.
- `handler.ts` line with `req.headers["x-ledger-secret"] ? "" : process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET!` is a serious bug candidate: if a request includes an `x-ledger-secret` header, the secret used for verification becomes the empty string `""`. An attacker can compute HMAC with an empty key. That's an auth bypass, pending confirmation.
